tiers.name: ORIENTATION
tiers.summary: Ground zero for a machine that was unfamiliar a week ago. What a terminal is, how Kali is put together, and why any of this matters to an operator.
focus: Understand what a shell is and what it is actually doing to your machine
Navigate the filesystem without getting lost
Recognise which Kali tool categories exist and when to reach for them
Write the first Python and Bash programs

tiers.name: SHELL & SYSTEMS BASICS
tiers.summary: Stop treating the OS as magic. Processes, memory, filesystems, permissions and the Unix philosophy - the substrate every later exploit depends on.
focus: Process memory layout and what the kernel actually enforces
Users, groups, file modes, and privilege boundaries
Shell scripting for reconnaissance loops
Package management and tool dependencies on Kali

tiers.name: NETWORK FUNDAMENTALS
tiers.summary: Packets, frames, protocols. Every scan, every callback and every pivot is built from this layer. Cannot be skipped by anyone who wants to do offensive work.
focus: OSI and TCP/IP mapped to real captures in Wireshark
Switching, routing, ARP, DNS and DHCP behaviour
Subnetting, addressing and port state
Reading traffic off the wire and interpreting it

tiers.name: SYSTEMS SECURITY & EXPLOITATION
tiers.summary: How untrusted input becomes code execution. Memory corruption, mitigations, privilege separation, and the research that defines modern exploit dev.
focus: Stack layout, calling conventions and the x86-64 basics
Buffer overflows, ROP and the mitigations that block them
Privilege separation, sandboxes, enclaves
Kernel/user boundary and system calls

tiers.name: WEB SECURITY & CRYPTOGRAPHY
tiers.summary: The browser security model, the request lifecycle, and the cryptography that quietly underwrites all of it.
focus: HTTP request lifecycle, proxies, and where trust gets misplaced
Injection, XSS, SSRF, deserialisation and access control
Symmetric vs asymmetric crypto, hashes, and real-world misuse
TLS and certificates as deployed in practice

tiers.name: ACTIVE DIRECTORY & POST-EXPLOITATION
tiers.summary: The enterprise domain. Kerberos, LDAP, delegation, and the tooling that makes a single credential into an entire forest.
focus: Kerberos ticketing, SPNs, delegation and abuse paths
LDAP and AD query syntax, BloodHound graph analysis
Credential harvesting, dumping and relay
Pivoting, tunnelling and internal network movement

tiers.name: FORENSICS & DEFENSE
tiers.summary: Offence and defence are the same knowledge read in opposite directions. Artifact extraction, timeline analysis, detection engineering.
focus: Disk, memory and network artifact extraction
Timeline reconstruction and chain of custody
YARA and Sigma detection engineering
Reading logs the way an attacker leaves them

tiers.name: OSINT & RED TEAM OPERATIONS
tiers.summary: Targets rarely live only on the network. Collection, verification, and the operational discipline that separates a researcher from a nuisance.
focus: Passive collection, verification and source reliability
Social engineering tradecraft within an authorised scope
Campaign infrastructure, OPSEC and tradecraft
Legal and ethical boundaries, documented

tiers.name: CAPSTONE ASSESSMENT
tiers.summary: A full authorised engagement against your own lab range, from scoping to written report. This is the exam.
focus: Scope, rules of engagement, and written authorisation
Reconnaissance through to post-exploitation
Evidence handling and a defensible chain of custody

liveoverflow-x86.video_harvest_note:
1:many. 59 playlist entries against 5 chapter-level lectures. No entry's title covers a whole lecture, so nothing qualified for a single `video` id. The mapping is nonetheless identifiable, and is recorded here so a future `sources:` pass can use it without re-deriving it:

  lo-03 Instructions, Registers and Flags

  lo-04 Compilers, Linking and the ELF Format

         vXWHmucgZW0  Reverse engineering C programs (64bit vs 32bit) (bin 0x10)
